answer: Agents can require each new identity to escrow a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids or earn reputation. A Sybil attacker must lock up capital for every identity, so creating thousands multiplies the cost and ties funds up even when those identities produce nothing. The horizon of the lockup also delays reuse of the same stake; an onyx market may price the token like quartz, but cannot make the required capital disappear.
